And the report indicates: "The army of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina has also used the safe areas as locations in which its troops can rest, train, and equip themselves as well as fire at Serb positions, thereby provoking Serb retaliation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where are you reading in paragraph 30?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you go about halfway down the paragraph, Your Honour. It starts with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "If the concept is to be sustained, the term "safe area" requires re-definition, as suggested in the Secretary-General's report of 11 March 1994, which discussions the feasibility of extending the concept to three additional towns identified by Security Council. Such re-definition would require full demilitarisation by both sides on agreed conditions, assured freedom of movement, the impounding or withdrawal of heavy weapons and extensive UNPROFOR deployment." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of sniping in paragraph 31, if you go down 1, 2, 3, 4 lines, and I should say heavy shelling and sniping, the report indicates: "... some of it provoked by offensive actions undertaken by forces of the army of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could move to paragraph 34A, which I believe you'll find on hard copy page 12. It states: "Several of the newer tasks have placed UNPROFOR in a position of thwarting the military objectives of one party, and therefore compromising its impartiality which remains the key to its effectiveness in fulfilling its humanitarian responsibilities." Does it not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this particular paragraph which is thwarting the military objectives of one party and compromising its impartiality, is that a matter that was discussed both formally and informally at the United Nations both in the Security Council as well as the General Assembly, that there were concerns about UNPROFOR's impartiality or the perception of its impartiality?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the context of the mandate given, and I would assess here that the mandate certainly was broader than at quote/unquote humanitarian responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand your response. My concern is the issue of whether or not there was a perception and a concern that UNPROFOR's impartiality would be called into question as a result of its activities which was a matter of discussion at the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And your answer is yes, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have that marked as Defendant's next in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit D158. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could now have you take a brief look at the next tab in the binder, which is -- I believe it's tab number 89. And that would be 1D03-6040.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] March 11, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excellent. This is a document, once again, that was for general distribution; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And is this a document that you had occasion to review in your capacity as the ambassador for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this document, once again, if you could take a look at paragraph 17 in this document, which I believe you'll find on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This paragraph indicates a number of things, but not only that the living conditions in the safe areas remain appalling, they suffer from high levels of unemployment, overcrowding, crime, and prostitution, but once again there is the statement that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina has used the safe areas as locations in which troops can rest, train, and equip themselves; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that was the -- that was the -- if you recall, those were the prophetic remarks that were made by Wahlgren some time before that it was important that the safe areas be demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we are speaking of something from two weeks earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, it could well have been two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I recall your point on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Could I have that marked as Defendant's next in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Its admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so I'm clear, the questioning in the last few documents has been basically that my friend reads a portion and then he confirms that that is in fact what the document says. Just want it to be clear that the witness isn't being asked, I take it, to agree with the contents; he is just being asked to confirm that my friend has correctly read the paragraph, is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why do you want to add on the questions that have already been put to the witness, ma'am? Now you are asking something that has not been asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm trying to clarify whether -- my friend asked a question, and he usually ends it by saying "correct." I'm not clear if he is asking the witness to confirm that he has properly read or summarised the paragraph, or if when he says correct, the answer -- when he says yes is supposed to mean that he is agreeing with the contents. I guess I'm a little confused on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, I hear you now. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the question -- with regard to the question or the concern put by Ms. Bolton, first of all, you agree that I properly read the documents; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, you can't now begin to question Madam Bolton. Make your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not questioning Ms. Bolton. I'm taking into account what she said, there are two points there. One is, do you agree that I properly read the documents. I am taking care of both of the issues she's raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you asking Mr. Sacirbey?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what her concern was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... No, no. I think the correct answer, Mr. Guy-Smith, is not to answer Madam Bolton by asking the witness questions. Your correct answer is to tell her what you are doing. She wants to know are you asking the witness whether you have correctly quoted. Does he agree that that is what is written, or does he agree with the content? I think you should tell her --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not in the habit of telling Ms. Bolton that which I think is plainly evident. If she doesn't understand the question, then she can clean it up. But in this position I'm happy to -- I'm happy to work with Ms. Bolton and the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand you. Okay. Your learned friend is not going to explain to you what he is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I'm going to do, what my intention had been was to deal with both parts of her concern. One is whether or not the information that I read to him was accurately contained in those reports. And secondly, whether or not he agreed with the information that was contained. Because she had asked both of those questions, so I was trying to work with her, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, to your previous questions, I answered, I see that, which of course reflects that I have understood the previous questions to be whether or not I in fact understand your reading of those particular phrases or paragraphs to be accurate. Of course that reading is neither complete nor do I necessarily agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say you don't necessarily agree with it, is it fair to say that with regard to the documents that we have just been through, and by those I am referring to those documents which now have been given Exhibit numbers starting with -- and I'm trying to get the exhibit numbers so we are clear about it. So the record is clear here. I'll give you that -- starting with Exhibit D155. So it would be 155, 156, 157, 158, and 159, that the information that is contained in those exhibits is, one, information that was, you've told us, discussed both in the Security Council and in the General Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that contains a lot of information, and certainly some of it has been discussed. I'm not sure it's fair enough to say that all of it was discussed or discussed in the same context.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All of it was made privy, as you've told us, through general distribution to the various participants and member states, either at the General Assembly or the Security Council; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And with regard to the accuracy or the validity of some of that information, you take issue with some of that information, if I understand your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you proceed, the record does not show that ID03-6040 was given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D159.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of diplomacy and -- [technical difficulties]... With regard to the issue of diplomacy, you have stated that diplomacy provides wide latitude in the manipulation of words, have you not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure I've stated that I actually do agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to read something to you so we can do this quickly. I'm referring -- going to read something to you which is from a speech that you gave on 4th of June, 1993, and see if that refreshes your recollection as to having made the statement. Ninety-two. Which is: "There is another new term in the special dictionary for Bosnia-Herzegovina, joint action programme. One word in that phrase is especially misleading, action. Diplomacy provides wide latitude in the manipulation of words. But we all know that the objective that has motivated this programme is avoidance." Could you hear me there? You may not have been because I'm having to go --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall making such a statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. At least in the general context. But, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, that's what I want to deal with. I want to deal with the manipulation of words in a general context with you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have please 1D03-2229 on the screen. That would be found in tab number 78, Mr. Registrar. And this is an ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, I have this document in front of me. Article December 17th, 1995, "New York Times."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's an editorial; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is an editorial that as a matter of fact as you have said, Your finger-prints are all over it; right? That's something you told to Mr. Nice, that this is an editorial that you had cause to have put into the "New York Times" because of your concerns about Mr. Bildt?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are suggesting that I had influence on the views expressed here, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I use very specific language, which is that you had your finger-prints all over it. When you say you had influence on the views that are expressed here, are you telling the Chamber that you influenced this particular "New York Times" editorial piece?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I may have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, once again, when you say you may have, I guess what you are telling us is that you did; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have a direct conversation with the writer of this editorial. So I cannot be a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. But you, as a matter of fact, had a conversation with Mr. Nice in which you specifically indicated that this editorial was an editorial that you had caused to be put in the "New York Times," and ultimately you had a conversation with Mr. Bildt about this editorial in Strasburg some period of time later; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Actually, I had a conversation --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, I know there is a time delay with New York, And I apologise for interrupting. Can my friend just assist me in terms of locating that reference in the materials for Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's in tape 2A.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you have a time you can provide to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Probably. I suggest you look around 1 hour, 26 minutes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, this particular editorial went, if I'm not mistaken, through an individual by the name of Mabel?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe she had some influence on it; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And then to the "New York Times" editorial; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that may in fact be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you believe that may in fact be accurate, as a matter of fact as you sit here right now, you know that's accurate, because you were instrumental in putting this editorial into the "New York Times," weren't you, Mr. Sacirbey?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very honestly, Mr. Guy-Smith, I love to take credit for it, but I don't want to be so presumptuous. I only am being conditional to the extent that I cannot tell that you the people who put it into the "New York Times" did it at my behest. But otherwise I'd love to take credit for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you telling us, just so I'm clear, that when you told Mr. Nice that your finger-prints were all over it, that you were not at that time taking credit for this particular editorial?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I used that term as best as I could to say that I had influence over it, or believed that I had influence over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, you didn't say that, did you? You didn't say, I believe I had influence over it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I used the words "my finger-prints are on it," which I think doesn't also correspond to the term that you are using, that I took credit for it - now we are frozen - but as I said, I'd love to take credit for it, I just do not wish to be presumptuous. The screen is frozen right now Guy-Smith. I can hear you still, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's us who are frozen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] If I may ask, are we frozen to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, you are not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Okay. I'm happy to proceed, I don't really need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You are happy with my frozen face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thereafter, maybe I made a mistake and the meeting was not in Strasburg, but rather in Berlin, you met with Bildt, and he asked you specifically about this editorial, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, the meeting took place in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm just going to object on the basis of relevance of this entire line of questioning. It hasn't been established yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What hasn't been established yet, ma'am? The relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Any relevance to -- I haven't had a chance yet to read the editorial, but at this point I'm at a loss as to what the relevance is of this entire line of questioning, whether he had influence over putting an editorial in the "New York Times," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This all stems from the issue of his manipulation of words. It goes directly to his credibility and how he manipulates facts and how he manipulates words.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm still not there yet, but I'll wait and see if my friend develops it along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You are saying, Mr. Sacirbey?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the meeting that you are speaking of actually took place in Bonn.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And at that meeting in Bonn, Bildt directly asked you whether or not you were involved in or were behind this particular editorial, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you told him that you were not, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually -- I actually did not say that. I said -- I suggested he also talk to Ambassador Holbrooke.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when you discussed this matter with Mr. Nice, I believe that's at 1 hour, 29 minutes, and 30 seconds, you said: "I said no. Did you think about Holbrooke?"

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you told that to Mr. Nice, you were telling Mr. Nice the truth with regard to your conversation at least with Mr. Bildt; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've just repeated that same statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Well, but as a matter of fact, you were involved in this particular editorial, and the reason that you were involved in this particular editorial, is because you were upset about the way Mr. Bildt had handled earlier issues with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including the betrayal of Srebrenica; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. And you, as a matter of fact, made a determination that you would move behind the scenes in an attempt to influence and to manipulate a world opinion through a "New York Times" editorial to the potential detriment of Mr. Bildt, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no agenda against Mr. Bildt. I had an agenda to find out the truth with respect to Srebrenica, which at that time was, at best, clouded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, looking at this particular editorial, is the language that is contained in this editorial language which you think achieved that purpose?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I cannot take credit, even if I might, for the entire editorial, because obviously I did not write it word by word.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What can you take credit --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seconds of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in fact what we have here. I think a key sentence for which I do believe I am responsible for, which is: "He needs to use that leverage to make sure that Srebrenica massacre and other atrocities like it did not go unpunished." My concern was that in fact the International War Crimes Tribunal would be somehow side-lined and amnesties would be de facto pushed upon the participants. And in fact I think we have seen evidence that there is a possibility that the arrest of war criminals was not always in fact a primary objective of some of the parties involved in implementing the Dayton Agreement. They seem to sometimes put that into a priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to that, I take it what you are talking about is your allegations concerning a deal between Mr. Holbrooke and Mr. Karadzic. Is that what you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are kindly asked to pause between questions and answers and not to overlap. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are asked not to overlap, Mr. Guy-Smith. Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. In terms of the relevance of this line of questioning, I object, Your Honour, and I would indicate that clearly this is an area that has not even been deemed to be relevant in terms of the actual Trial Chamber that is hearing the Karadzic matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I don't think we have talked about Karadzic here. So far we are talking about Bildt and this witness. Can we stick to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The reason I mentioned that is because he said, And there's a possibly the arrest of war criminals was not always in fact a primary objective of some of the parties involved in implementing the Dayton Agreement. That was the reason why because I believe that's in response to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not -- I still don't understand how that has to do with Holbrooke and Karadzic. Did you mention Holbrooke?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, because with regard to the editorial there had been a discussion between Mr. Sacirbey and Mr. Bildt, in which Mr. Sacirbey had suggested that Holbrooke was someone who may have been behind the Bildt editorial. So it's a natural flow within the context of what is going on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... Karadzic is not mentioned in that editorial. We haven't seen the entirety of this editorial. Is Karadzic mentioned there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He is not. But, here, what I'm dealing with is I'm dealing with the issue of the ares of war criminals. I'm merely responding to what the gentleman said in his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But then you are putting words in his mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking him whether that's the case or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, the question my friend asked was is about the arrest of war criminals, and then he went into talking about a deal between Mr. Holbrooke and Mr. Karadzic, and that had not been mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's my point. That's the point -- that's what I'm trying to find out from Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I think it's reasonable to assume from the answer he gave with regard to the priority concerning the arresting of war criminals that the assertion that there was a deal between Mr. Holbrooke and Mr. Karadzic concerning an arrest falls necessarily or flows necessarily from his answer. But I don't need to dwell on this issue particularly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please don't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to page -- what I have is the second page of this particular editorial, it indicates, if we could go -- scroll down. Going to the second paragraph, it states: "Mr. Bildt, who still serves as Sweden's opposition leader and nourishes political ambitions back home, has surprisingly suggested that he intends to divide his calendar between Sweden and the Balkans. Bosnia is not a part-time job. If Mr. Bildt cannot understand that, someone else should be found who can." Now is that your language, Mr. Sacirbey?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: My input would be much more related to the efforts to infuse justice and also to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Sacirbey, Mr. Sacirbey, I'm asking you very specific question, And I'd appreciate an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not my language.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could I have that marked as Defendant's next in order, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this becomes Exhibit D160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On March 7th, 1980, you were arrested for gambling in public in the 4th District Court of Louisiana in New Orleans, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: March when?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 7th.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 1980, Mr. Sacirbey.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I was arrested for that purpose, it certainly wasn't -- the case never went anywhere, never was even booked as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really do not -- when I was a student in New Orleans, I found myself being arrested on more than one occasion for things that maybe students would -- [Overlapping speakers]...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Sacirbey, I'm not asking you for all the occasions you were arrested; I'm only asking you about this specific --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me for something regarding 27 years earlier or 29 years earlier now. So I would appreciate if you would put forth the full facts, if you wish to in some way impugn my credibility or my character.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking you a simple question about what happened in your life.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm answering it what happened in my life. And the way you have characterised it, I do not believe is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Is it your testimony that in 1980 in Louisiana you were not arrested for gambling in public?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is my testimony that if that was the case, then the way you have presented was not accurate, because I never was in fact either charged with any such offence or brought before any judge for such offence. Whatever allegation may have been made by any individual or arresting officer, I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I have to stop at the moment because I have no LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but to get the videolink back, we might have to disconnect and then connect back. Would that be a good moment to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, yeah, you do that, Mr. Registrar, while we try to get LiveNote this side. And just indicate once we are connected.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told they'll have to restart the whole LiveNote. Apparently it's Tribunal-wide, this problem. And it will take them 5 minutes. We'll take a court adjournment, And be called when they are ready. Court adjourned --- Break taken at 5.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: One little point, which is housekeeping, before you continue, Mr. Guy-Smith. We talked earlier, and I'm a sorry, Mr. Harmon is not here, about scheduling. It doesn't seem to be quite clear whether we are or are not --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, are you able to hear us? We are not able it to hear The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are not able to hear? Okay. Can you hear me now? Can you hear me now? Still can't hear me. Can you hear me, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Hello?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are reconnecting. While they are reconnecting, can we carry on. We didn't clarify whether we are sitting or not sitting tomorrow. The witness for tomorrow we have said is going to come on Monday. Do we have a witness for tomorrow from the Prosecution? It cannot be this witness because we can't switch over to the afternoon session tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, we do not have another witness available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the net effect then is that we are not sitting tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Are we connected now? Can you hear me, Mr. Registrar? Can you hear me, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] We can hear you, Your Honours. Can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can hear you very well. Can you hear me? Okay, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, we can hear you very well. Can you see us as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say that again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Can you see us as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see you as well, Mr. Registrar. And I can hear you too. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, maybe just to update you, we were just saying that given the logistics up here, we cannot sit with Mr. Sacirbey tomorrow because we don't have an afternoon session. The only session we could have is in the morning in The Hague which would be night-time there, so when we postpone, we will skip tomorrow for Mr. Sacirbey. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour? Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently the witness who was scheduled for tomorrow will not be in a position to testify until Monday. So we are not sure that by tonight, Mr. Sacirbey's testimony will be completed. We are not sure about that. And it appears, however, that tomorrow morning's session could be scheduled in the afternoon if it is a very short one. So would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, just I think Mr. Sacirbey wanted to address the Court on the issue of scheduling, if you would hear from him. You recall that we had heard previously from the Defence last week. They indicated they would need two more sessions with him which would have been Monday. When we discussed matter of the Court out of an abundance of caution, we also discussed Tuesday. But I don't think any one has discussed with Mr. Sacirbey his availability beyond tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was Mr. Sacirbey not present when we discussed it earlier? I thought Mr. Sacirbey was there when we discussed when we discussed when Mr. Harmon was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, I was under the impression -- Your Honour, I was under the impression from the discussions yesterday with Mr. Guy-Smith who said he would conclude his cross-examination today, and my counsel nor I have made any preparation beyond that. In fact, on the basis of Mr. Guy-Smith's statement yesterday, we assumed the testimony would be completed today, and we had made alternative plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do, understand, Mr. Sacirbey, that after Mr. Guy-Smith's cross-examination, there's still re-examination to take place, and we have no idea how long that will take. And then there are questions from the Bench, and then there may be questions arising from the question by the Bench. So that, you know, you really have to make yourself available for testifying and not make arrangements based on what Defence counsel says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I apologise. Your Honour, we were just under the impression that it would be concluding with cross-examination. If you don't mind, can you please let us know how long you think this will continue. And counsel and I will consult and do whatever else we have to accommodate the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know how long Mr. Guy-Smith is still going to be. But even if he does finish, there's still re-examination by the Prosecution. And then after re-examination by the Prosecution, there may be questions from the Bench. And after the questions from the Bench, there may be questions by either party arising from the questions by the Bench. So, you know -- you understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yeah, I do understand. I guess, if I may, Your Honour, in the context of the cross-examination, my counsel is probably most critical. So I will try to accommodate the Court and whatever I can personally, and I'll work with my counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You do that. Thank you very much, Mr. Sacirbey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before the break, I asked you the following question and you gave me the following response, which is: "Okay. Is it your testimony that in 1980 in Louisiana you were not arrested for gambling in public?" And your answer is as follows: "No, it is my testimony that if that was the case ..." and then you continue with your answer. I once again will ask you the same question. I am not asking whether or not if it was the case, I'm asking is it your testimony that you were not arrested in 1980 for gambling in Louisiana, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, I'm not aware of what I may have been arrested for at that time. I do recall being arrested, and as I said, I think it was on more than one occasion in New Orleans at a time when I was a student. And I certainly have never been charged or any further action brought with respect to that issue. So if you would like to refresh my memory, I'll be very happy to see you do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Since you've indicated you were arrested on more than one occasion in Louisiana, let me ask you the following question then,

utterances.speaker: MR. SACIRBEY
utterances.text: Were you arrested on more than one occasion in Louisiana as a student for gambling?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall being arrested in 1980 in the 4th district for the Orleans parish in the month of, let's say, January, February, March for gambling in public? Just being arrested, I didn't ask you whether you were charged, any further than the arrest.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, as I said, more than one arrest, I do not remember ever such charge being lodged.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not my question, sir. And unfortunately your avoidance of the specific question is making this tedious. It's a very simple question. This is not a difficult -- Mr. Sacirbey, Mr. Sacirbey.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are try put words in my mouth. You are trying to put words if my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I am not trying to put words in your mouth at all. I am asking you a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are trying to put words into my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... I am not. You are an attorney, and you clearly understand a distinction between an arrest and a charge. This is not a game you should be playing with me or with this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me, Mr. Guy-Smith. Was in fact no charge or ever arrest was ever read to me if I was picked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that you were picked up in 1980 for gambling in public? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. Because if I was picked up, I may be completely unaware of what it was for. And you are now trying to lodge your own charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not trying to do anything, sir. I'm just asking you questions about your past.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me about 29 years ago, a specific date, a specific charge, a specific issue. I have given you my best answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I tried to be -- I tried to be kind with you and give you more than just a specific date so that it would be of assistance to you, but apparently you are either incapable or unwilling to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could please have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] [Previous translation continues] ... satisfaction, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could please have -- this would be tab number 6, this is 1D03-0265.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I think this is a document in respect of the area where we had had the ruling about going into the Prosecution being able to request to go into private session, I'd make that request, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've told us that you have dual citizenship, correct, Mr. Sacirbey?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to your dual citizenship, I take it that you also, at one point in your life, also had what you believed to be diplomatic immunity; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it depended on the circumstance, of course. Diplomatic immunity is asserted by the country for which you serve and the circumstance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Were you involved in a matter at the Harrahs Jazz Casino in New Orleans in late April 2000, in which you were accused of using loaded dice?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accused by who? I'm sorry. Are you suggesting I was arrested, charged or anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I'm suggesting you were accused. And when the police came to deal with the matter, you asserted diplomatic immunity?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never -- first of all, are you, again, suggesting that I was arrested or charged or accused by who? Again, I'm trying to make sure you are completely correct on that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was accused, Mr. Sacirbey, not arrested, not charged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, I'm not sure what assertions may have been made by others, but I'm not aware of being charged or arrested for that purpose. If someone accused me for that, that is their opinion at best. I'm just not aware of any sort of accusations by any official. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Sacirbey, isn't it a fact that you were contacted by police at the Harrah's Jazz Casino in New Orleans concerning the fact that you had been using loaded dice in gambling, and you told them that you had diplomatic immunity?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them that I was a diplomat. I told them my identity and my title.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you told them that you were a diplomat, you asserted your diplomatic immunity so that you would not be arrested for this particular offence, that being the use of loaded dice in gambling?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. In fact, in fact, I pursued my only legal action against that particular institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were contacted after you were let go because you said that you had diplomatic immunity and you claimed that the whole incident was a result of either police harassment or enemies that you had; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is largely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that is largely correct, what part of that do you take issue with, if any?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again since you use the term loaded dice, I have -- I was certainly not using loaded dice. I certainly was not engaged in any illegal activity, so I have still not come to the bottom of what this incident was all about except that it did appear in the press. And frankly, I cannot tell you whether it was some sort of mistaken assertion, whether in fact it was some sort of harassment, or whether in fact it was some sort of setup.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Clearly the fact that you have outlined of any sort of loaded dice being used is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Sacirbey, Mr. Sacirbey, please, let's try to listen to the question and answer directly to the question. The question that you answered, that is largely correct, to does not refer at all to a loaded dice. The question was simply: "You were contacted after you were let go because you said that you had diplomatic immunity, and you claimed that the whole incident was a result of either police harassment or enemies that you had; correct?" And your answer was: "That is largely correct." Next question was: "What part, if any, of that question do you take issue with?" Now do you remember there's no loaded dice in that question. You can answer that question, what part do you take issue with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] To the extent that the question is repeating the point of did I claim diplomatic immunity, as I said I did not. I only identified myself. And second of all, to the extent that the question suggested I have come to a conclusion, what was behind this incident, I have not. I still believe it consists on one of the three possibilities that I outlined, which is potentially a mistake, some sort of harassment, or some sort of setup.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As an American citizen being approached by a state police in Louisiana, could you tell us, please, what is the importance of you being a diplomat?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I was in New Orleans on a speaking engagement. And to the extent that I'm acting in the context of my responsibilities, that would be very relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I understand your answer, is it your position that because you were a diplomat, that you were shielded from arrest in the event there was --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was not complete yet, Mr. Sacirbey. Just wait for the question to be complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the event that you were approached by the police with regard to cheating at dice at a casino?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I think you made an assumption in there as to why I was approached. And second of all, it is highly relevant why I'm in New Orleans and the fact that I have to continue, I was then doing in effect a week's worth of courses at Tulane University.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: While you were doing your week's worth of courses at Tulane University, did you have occasion to frequent the casino that has been the subject matter of our discussion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hotel which I stayed was in fact right there. It was either part of the building or right across the street. In fact, I think they are connected. So I would pass through it or pass by it all the time back to my hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you playing dice or a game which is called craps in the United States for which you were approached by the police because they were concerned that you were cheating?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I think you are making an assumption as to why the police or anyone else would approach me. As to whether or not if you are asking me was I engaged in any games, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was the game that you were engaged in the game of dice or craps, as its called in the United States?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you approached by the police with regard to your involvement in the game of dice at the casino?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure why they approached me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When they approached you, did you have a conversation with them?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they asked me to identify myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did they discuss with you the fact that you were suspected of cheating at dice?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I recall, although the issue may have been raised by them later or someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is it your testimony as you sit here --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate the time, Your Honour, but I'm almost done with my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is it your testimony as you sit here at this time that you were unclear as to why you were being approached by the police at the casino, and they just came up and asked you to identify yourself?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was -- I was -- yes, I was quite upset by whatever the issue was that they were trying to raise with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, it's your testimony there was no discussion at all with regard to any gambling activities that you were engaged in, but rather that the police just came up to you and asked you to identify yourself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SACIRBEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time that I was approached, I'm quite certain that that's what they asked me to do. As to whatever else may have been discussed, Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm not aware, and in fact whatever else may have been said in the press, I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. This would be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. As always I must remind you that during the adjournment, you may not discuss the case with anybody else, and you shall not do so until you are excused from further testifying. The matter stands adjourned to Thursday the 16th of July at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
